## Upgrading from v0.5.0

**`lift` takes `-r/--ir` in place of `-l/--lifter-type`, and names a
representation rather than a tool.** `-l ghidra` becomes `-r ghidra-pcode`.
The values are `ghidra-pcode`, `ida-microcode` and `binary-ninja-llil` /
`-mlil` / `-hlil`; as before, only Ghidra's is implemented, and the others
report which representation was refused.

Nothing about the file format changed. A program lifted by v0.5.0 carries
`"ir": "ghidra-pcode"` and reads exactly as it did.

`LifterType` is gone from the library's public API, and `LifterBuilder::new`
takes an `Ir`. `AnyProgram` has gained three variants, so a `match` over it in
downstream code needs three more arms.

angr is gone from that list as well. It never lifted anything — it parsed,
and then reported that the angr lifter was not implemented — so the only
scripts it can break are ones that were already failing.

## Highlights

- **Binary Ninja lifts, to all three of its intermediate languages.**
  `-r binary-ninja-llil`, `-mlil` or `-hlil`. Which one answers a question is
  not something a tool should decide, so all three are offered and none is
  recommended; they are different vocabularies rather than different amounts
  of one, and birthmarks are not compared across them.

  It runs through `bnpython3`, Binary Ninja's own interpreter, which has the
  API importable already, so nothing touches your `python3` or `PYTHONPATH`.
  `BINARY_NINJA_HOME`, `--home`, and the usual install locations work as they
  do for Ghidra.

  The symbol table each file carries is keyed by whatever its level renders a
  call target as: an address at LLIL and MLIL, the callee's own name at HLIL,
  which has already resolved it.

  Binary Ninja is licensed and cannot be installed on a CI runner, so nothing
  in CI lifts with it. Its script is parsed on every push, and fixtures under
  `testdata/hello_world/bnil/` are read back — including an assertion that
  each level finds the call that is in them, since a reader recognising none
  of its own call operations would report unrelated programs as identical.

- **The representation is the only thing you name.** `lift` used to take both
  a tool and, in the plan for Binary Ninja, a level within it — two arguments
  that could contradict each other, so something would have had to check for
  a combination that only existed because there were two of them. There is one
  now, and `-l ghidra --il hlil` cannot be written down.

  A representation implies its tool; a tool does not imply a representation,
  since Binary Ninja has three. Keeping the tool as the argument would have
  kept the one that cannot answer the question being asked — which reader can
  read this file, and may these two birthmarks be compared.

  Binary Ninja's three levels are declared here even though nothing lifts to
  them yet, the way `ida-microcode` already was.

- angr is no longer an advertised lifter. It was declared early, ahead of any
  work on it, and stayed a name in a list whose only reachable outcome was an
  error. It comes back when there is something behind it.

  Removing it also removed the only backend with no installation directory, so
  `home_spec` stops returning an `Option` and `find_home` loses the branch that
  said `--home` means nothing here. Neither could be reached once angr was the
  only case, and an unreachable error path is one nothing keeps honest.
- The install page names the JDK Ghidra actually needs. It said "typically JDK
  17 or later"; Ghidra 12 refuses 17, and the repository's other two statements
  of the requirement — the lifter's README and the `full` container image —
  already said 21. Following the install page led to a failure whose message,
  `Unable to prompt user for JDK path, no TTY detected`, says nothing about
  versions at all, so the page now names that symptom too.
- The publication list in the README runs newest first, the way the site's
  Academic page already did, and both gain a submission to the International
  Journal of Software Innovation on how statically linked libraries distort
  cross-platform birthmark similarity.
